quote: I believe that in about fifty years' time it will be possible, to programme computers, with a storage capacity of about 109, to make them play the imitation game so well that an average interrogator will not have more than 70 per cent chance of making the right identification after five minutes of questioning.
how_tested: Imitation game: can a judge tell machine from human in conversation?
public_note: “109” is 10^9 in the original; the superscript is lost in the source text. Proposed as a test of whether machines can think, not of general intelligence. Judges, duration and pass mark vary from one run to the next.
notes: Same quote and source as claims.csv gr02, already verified.

quote: These are then mathematically formalised to produce a general measure of intelligence for arbitrary machines.
how_tested: An agent's expected performance summed over all computable environments, weighted toward simpler ones.
public_note: The most formally precise definition, but the sum runs over every computable environment, so it cannot be computed in practice.

quote: highly autonomous systems that outperform humans at most economically valuable work
how_tested: No test named; would need a measure of 'most economically valuable work'.
ARC-AGI puzzles (scores in Measured on this page).
public_note: Defines intelligence, not AGI as such; ARC was built to measure it.
notes: Abstract, 'On the Measure of Intelligence', submitted 2019-11-05.

quote: This framework introduces levels of AGI performance, generality, and autonomy
how_tested: Rates systems by depth (performance) and breadth (generality); no fixed test battery.
public_note: Treats AGI as a ladder of levels rather than one threshold.
notes: Abstract, 'Levels of AGI for Operationalizing Progress on the Path to AGI', v1 2023-11-04.

who: Dan Hendrycks, Dawn Song et al.
quote: defining AGI as matching the cognitive versatility and proficiency of a well-educated adult ... The resulting AGI scores (e.g., GPT-4 at 27%, GPT-5 at 57%)
how_tested: Ten cognitive domains from Cattell-Horn-Carroll theory, scored with adapted human test batteries; 100% = AGI.
public_note: The closest to an objective, scored definition. Scores in the quote are the paper's own, as of its writing.
notes: Abstract, 'A Definition of AGI', v1 2025-10-21, v3 2025-12-03.

quote: Once AGI is declared by OpenAI, that declaration will now be verified by an independent expert panel.
how_tested: Declared by OpenAI, verified by a panel; no public criterion.
public_note: Both companies' announcements of the 2026-04-27 amendment do not mention AGI. Secondary reports say the AGI clause was dropped then; that is not confirmed by either company.
notes: Checked openai.com/index/next-phase-of-microsoft-partnership and blogs.microsoft.com 2026-04-27 post: zero AGI mentions (2026-10-29).

who: Manifold markets plotted on this page
quote: AGI can theoretically perform any intellectual task that a human being can
how_tested: A market moderator judges whether a system qualifies.
public_note: The four AGI markets in Crowd vs. CEOs share this wording. Their odds are odds on a moderator's judgement, not on a test result.
notes: Text from the market description via the Manifold API (2026-10-29).
